name: Dissolving copper(II) sulfate pentahydrate in water

time_constant_s.source: teaching-pace timescale, not a measured rate

observations.started: The blue crystals begin to dissolve and blue colour spreads into the water.
observations.saturated: No more copper sulfate dissolves: the solution is saturated and crystals remain at the bottom.
observations.completed: All the copper sulfate has dissolved. The solution is a uniform blue.

explanation: In water, each copper(II) ion (Cu²⁺) is surrounded by water molecules. These hydrated copper ions absorb light from the red end of the spectrum, so the solution looks blue. The more copper sulfate is dissolved, the deeper the blue.
